extracted.intended_audience: Aspiring authors (especially Australian/New Zealand residents) preparing submissions or query letters to Hachette Australia — particularly adult nonfiction and children's/YA authors
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on preparing an email submission/query and accompanying materials for Hachette Australia, including what to include in the cover letter, comps, synopsis, chapter outline and manuscript formats. Focused on making a submission that matches Hachette’s stated requirements and commercial expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the publisher's submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect and follow the guidelines on the publisher’s website exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher’s website sets out what information they need so they can decide whether the project is a fit. If Hachette states they are not accepting fiction submissions at the moment, they mean they are not accepting any fiction submissions, including yours. Move on rather than ignoring stated policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be a resident of Australia or New Zealand to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being disingenuous about your residency status wastes everybody's time. The site explicitly requires Australian or New Zealand residency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email subject line must include title and genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Put the book title and genre in the subject line of your submission email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for the publisher to identify what you are sending. The subject line is the first filter for inbox triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title: clarity, testing and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your title is extremely important — it’s the publisher’s first impression and must communicate or intrigue clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain a few responses to your working title from people other than friends and family before submitting. Review your title from the point of view of someone unfamiliar with the manuscript: does it mean to the reader what you think it means? Does it raise more questions than it answers?

rubrics_metrics.name: Be certain of genre and target age group
rubrics_metrics.description: Know and correctly identify the genre/age band of your manuscript before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you’re unsure about the genre of your work, it might not be ready. For children’s books, use standard age ranges (e.g., picture books, early reader, first chapter books, middle-grade 8–12, YA 12–18). Misclassifying (such as a 10,000-word 'picture book') signals you don’t know your audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter must contain required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover letter is the main section of your submission and must include specific components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As per Hachette’s submission guidelines, include: your contact details (professional email), a short summary (concise — no more than two paragraphs), the intended audience, comparable titles, a brief author bio, whether the manuscript is on submission elsewhere, and any required attachments. Make the publisher’s job easy so they will open and read your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short summary / synopsis in cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize your work concisely in the cover letter: no more than two paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concision is hard; have someone else edit. You must be able to summarize your work clearly and leave out nothing essential to the reader’s understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience — specific demographics and media habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the book’s target reader(s) precisely: demographics, media appetite and timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider age range, gender, location, relevant family/lifestyle characteristics, what TV/radio/podcasts they consume, and why now is the right time for this book. Your book is not 'for everyone' — paint a clear picture of the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable (comp) titles: selection and number
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide realistic comparison titles (comps) to show market placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick at least three to five comps, with at least two authors from your home market (for Hachette Australia, include relevant Australian projects). Preferably pick comps published in the last five years and avoid citing massive runaway bestsellers. Comps help publishers visualise how to present and shelve your book; be realistic (don’t claim your book is like 'nothing ever published').

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief author bio: relevant credits and platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a concise author bio that highlights publishing credits, media exposure or platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have publishing credits, relevant media appearances, an active social media presence, or a growing engaged email list, mention them. Do not invent credits or cite childhood prizes/encouragement awards. Publishers value direct-to-consumer marketing capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of other submissions / exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether your manuscript is already on submission elsewhere and be honest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t lie. Decide whether you are pursuing the agent route or direct-to-publisher route; querying publishers while waiting on agents can hamper your chances because agents can’t shop a manuscript already rejected by a publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments: required manuscript materials and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the attachments Hachette requests, in the correct formats and with required components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all submissions include a short synopsis and the total word count. Hachette asks for approximately a 300-word synopsis (about one to one-and-a-half pages double spaced). For children: submit a Word document or a low-res PDF of illustrated works. For adult nonfiction: provide a completed manuscript Word doc OR a detailed chapter outline plus the first 3,000 words (minimum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction: provide a detailed chapter outline
rubrics_metrics.description: If pitching nonfiction, include a detailed chapter-by-chapter outline that demonstrates the book’s argument and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers need to visualise the entire manuscript and be confident you have book-length material rather than an extended essay. The outline should demonstrate what’s different about your project and prove the structure and nature of your argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure word count fits genre expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your manuscript’s word count falls within typical ranges for its genre/format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research recommended word counts before submitting; eg. an illustrated picture book with 10,000 words signals a mismatch and will hurt your chances. Include the total word count in your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional presentation and external feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Present yourself professionally and have others review key elements (title, summary, synopsis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a professional-sounding email address; avoid jokey or off-putting addresses. Get people (not just friends/family) to respond to your title and edit your summary/synopsis. If unsure or you want personalised help, consider professional editorial/agent-query support.
